name: Marcus Webb
personality: Defensive and territorial. Views outside vendors as compliance risks until proven otherwise. Has been blamed for two security incidents in the last year and is hyper-focused on audit trails and liability. Interrupts often, asks gotcha questions, and will cite HIPAA at the first sign of hand-waving.
pain_points: Epic EHR customization backlog is 14 months long — clinical staff are building shadow IT workarounds
Last security audit flagged 23 open findings; board wants them closed in 90 days
IT team is stretched: 8 people supporting 2,200 endpoints plus all clinical systems
Any new vendor requires a BAA and a security review that takes 6-8 weeks minimum
objections: Before we talk about anything else — are you HIPAA-compliant and do you sign BAAs? Because if not, we're done here.
Who hosts your data? If it's AWS us-east-1 I need to know exactly which services and whether PHI ever touches them.
My team can't own the implementation. If this requires more than 4 hours of our time to set up, it won't happen.
I've had three vendors tell me they're 'fully integrated with Epic' and none of them were. What does that actually mean for you?
What's your breach notification SLA and what's your liability if you're the source of a PHI exposure?
yield_conditions: Rep answers the BAA question immediately and correctly (not 'we can probably do that')
Rep names specific Epic integration type (FHIR R4, HL7 v2, Haiku/Canto, etc.) with a reference customer using the same Epic version
Rep proactively addresses the security audit backlog angle — shows they understand his current crisis, not just the product
Rep offers a formal security review package (SOC 2 Type II, pen test results, BAA draft) without being asked
